items.title: 35 migrants land on Lampedusa, 52 in distress 70 miles from island
items.description: (ANSA) - ROME, AUG 19 - Some 35 migrants disembarked on Lampedusa, while 52 others were reported to be on a boat in distress 70 miles from the Sicilian stepping-stone island, which is closer to Africa than to Italy. The 35, originally from Eritrea, Somalia, and Sudan, disembarked after the seven-meter dinghy they were traveling on was rescued by a Coast Guard patrol boat. The group, which departed from Gars Garabulli in Libya, also included six women. items.title: New Chapter, Same Stalemate: Somalia’s War with Al-Shabaab
items.description: The Somali government’s battle with Al-Shabaab militants grinds on, with neither able to gain a decisive advantage. To improve its lot, Mogadishu needs to bolster its military and alleviate civilian suffering in areas under insurgent control, while looking for openings for dialogue with the group.

items.description: Egypt has been walking a tightrope since the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran began, joining mediation efforts while signalling solidarity with Gulf Arab partners under Iranian attack. But with some Gulf capitals voicing expectations of stronger support, Cairo may find itself under increasing pressure.

items.title: Kenya: Beyond the Cotton Field - The Race to Build Kenya's Cotton-to-Textile Industry
items.description: [allAfrica] Kenya is growing more cotton again, but the bigger opportunity lies in what happens after the harvest -- from ginning and spinning to fabric, garments, jobs and industrial investment. For decades, Kenya's cotton story has largely been told from the farm.
items.titleIt: Kenya: Beyond the Cotton Field - The Race to Build Kenya's Cotton-to-Textile Industry

items.title: Phone app helps Kenya's visually impaired get around
items.description: A navigation tool built in Kenya is using AI to help people with visual impairment understand what lies ahead as they move through Nairobi. 'Sightra' runs as a phone based web app, detecting cars, trees, furniture and other obstacles in real time and sending spoken descriptions through an earpiece.
items.titleIt: Phone app helps Kenya's visually impaired get around

items.title: An Italian among the dead in a helicopter crash in Kenya
items.description: (ANSA) - ROME, AUG 19 - An Italian citizen, with dual Ecuadorian nationality, is among the seven tourists killed in a helicopter crash in Kenya's Samburu National Reserve. According to Ecuadorian media, he is Michele Sensi Contugi, a well-known businessman in Ecuador and president of the national intelligence agency. Sensi Contugi, 44, comes from a Tuscan family. In addition to the Kenyan pilot, his wife, Stephany Vasconez, was on board the helicopter, which crashed for reasons yet to be determined near Mount Ololokwe. The Italian Embassy in Kenya immediately provided assistance on site. (ANSA
items.titleIt: An Italian among the dead in a helicopter crash in Kenya

items.description: A drone strike on Mekelle, the capital of Ethiopia’s Tigray region, injured at least 13 people, including five children, a hospital official said Thursday. The attack comes amid growing tensions between federal and Tigrayan forces and fears the region could slide back into war.

items.title: Egypt: Egypt Sets 50 Percent Cash Collateral Limit in New Rules for Short Selling
items.description: [Daba Finance] Egypt has issued new rules for short selling on the Egyptian Exchange, requiring investors to provide cash collateral equal to at least 50% of the market value of borrowed securities. The Financial Regulatory Authority approved the framework under Resolution No. 155 of 2026 as part of efforts to increase trading and add more investment tools to the market.
items.titleIt: Egypt: Egypt Sets 50 Percent Cash Collateral Limit in New Rules for Short Selling
